verdicts.title: Dashboard SAFETY card shows a green "Safe" badge while it is measuring nothing
verdicts.location_wrong: The cited unit/where (packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/dashboard/widgets/cockpit_run_controls.dart, 'dashboard/ weather/safety tile') contains NO weather or safety code. The real widget is RunDashboardWeatherSafetyCard at packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/sequencer/widgets/run_dashboard/weather_safety_card.dart:21-32, which the Dashboard mounts via packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/dashboard/widgets/dashboard_widget_registry.dart:500. A fixer following the stated path would find nothing.
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced live on a fresh v-wizards profile with no weather/safety device connected (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-14.png, vw-04.png): the SAFETY tile header carries a green check pill reading 'Safe' directly above 'Data  Unavailable', an amber 'No weather data sources available' banner, and 'Weather safety is off - conditions are not being checked'. Source confirms the mechanism and shows the team already knew: the pill is a bare switch on safety.status only (weather_safety_card.dart:21-32, WeatherSafetyStatus.safe => ('Safe', colors.success, LucideIcons.check)), while WeatherSafetyState carries a dedicated `monitoringEnabled` flag whose own doc comment at weather_safety_provider.dart:158-165 reads 'status falls through to WeatherSafetyStatus.safe purely because there is no verdict to report. UI must NOT render that as a green conditions-safe-for-imaging - it is not assessed. Surfaces read this flag to tell the two states apart.' This card never reads it, and never reads dataSource==unavailable either. Severity P1 stands: the body text does disclose the truth two lines down, which is the only thing keeping it out of P0.

verdicts.title: Tonight card reports a concrete twilight time and 9h28m imaging window while saying 'Location needed'
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced live: fresh profile, onboarding skipped, no site set. Dashboard -> Edit Dashboard -> Widgets -> Tonight. The card (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-14.png) reads Twilight 15:21, Moon 84%, Window 9h 28m, Target 'Location needed', Exposure '--', with the command bar LST showing '-:-:-' in the same frame. DB agrees: sqlite3 .../v-wizards/data/skotiq.db 'select key,value from app_settings where key like observer%' -> observer_latitude|0.0, observer_longitude|0.0, observer_elevation|0.0. I recomputed the numbers independently rather than trusting either readout: for lat 0 / lon 0 on 2026-08-02, sun altitude -18deg crossings are 19:22 UTC (dusk) and 04:51 UTC (dawn), i.e. 15:22 and 00:51 in this machine's local zone, giving a dark window of 9h29m. The app's 15:21/15:22 and 9h28m are exactly the equator-at-Greenwich values rendered in local time - so the finding's stated cause is correct, not just its symptom. Source confirms: tonight_card.dart:76-107 formats twilight.astronomicalDusk/Dawn with no location gate whatsoever; only Target (:69) and Exposure (:154) degrade to a placeholder. Severity P1 held: 'Window 9h 28m' is a number a user plans a night around and it is silently wrong for every observer not on the equator.

verdicts.title: Dashboard Capture card fires the OLD exposure while displaying the new one (typed value only commits on Enter)
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced exactly. Fresh v-wizards profile, Simulated Camera+Mount+Filter Wheel connected, Dashboard -> Edit Dashboard -> Widgets -> Capture Settings. Clicked the Exp box (default 120.0), Ctrl+A, typed 2, pressed Tab (focus visibly moved to Gain, field still read '2' - /tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-21.png), pressed Capture. app.log: 'Starting 120s exposure with gain=Some(100), offset=Some(50), bin=1x1'. /tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-22.png shows the card reading 'Exp: 2' beside a 10% ring - 10% of 120 s = 12 s, matching wall clock since the log line, so the ring is timing the 120 s run, not a 2 s one. Control: repeating with Enter instead of Tab renormalised the field to '3.0' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-23.png), i.e. the commit path works and only the blur path is missing. Cited location is correct: capture_settings_card.dart:536 is `onSubmitted: widget.onChanged` inside _CompactSettingField (class at :449), with no onEditingComplete, no onChanged and no FocusNode; didUpdateWidget at :478 only overwrites the controller when the provider value changes, so the stale text survives indefinitely. Both Exp and Gain use this field. P1 is right - it is silent and unbounded (the card can disagree with the hardware forever), but it needs a user to leave the field by blur rather than Enter, which keeps it below P0.

verdicts.title: All-Sky polar alignment reticle says "Within acceptance - hold steady" and 0.0" before a single frame has been taken
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced on the first try, fresh profile, no prior run to leak state. Imaging -> Mount -> Three-Point Polar Alignment -> All-Sky segment: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-27.png shows the intro copy ('Point at any bright star field...'), the footer 'Ready to start polar alignment' with a 'Start Alignment' button, Azimuth/Altitude/Total all '--', and in the same rail a green centred marker captioned '0.0"' / 'Within acceptance - hold steady'. No exposure and no solve had run. Contrast shot proving the mechanism: after pressing Start (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-28.png) the same reticle correctly reads 'Waiting for first plate solve...' - so the honest mode exists and is simply not used for the idle phase. Cause is precisely located but the actionable file is the CALLER, not the reticle: _right_panel.dart:24-31 passes `state.currentError?.azimuthError ?? 0.0` / `?? 0.0` and sets `waitingForFirstFrame: state.phase == PolarAlignPhase.adjusting && state.currentError == null`, so in the idle phase the flag is false and the widget computes totalError=0 <= threshold -> withinThreshold -> green marker + 'Within acceptance'. all_sky_target_reticle.dart:96-108 is only the renderer of that lie. Severity P1 held: an operator glancing at the rail can read a perfect polar alignment off a wizard that has measured nothing.

verdicts.title: Polar alignment computes and reports azimuth/altitude error at latitude 0, longitude 0 when no observing location is set
verdicts.reasoning: Every load-bearing link in the chain verified independently. (1) The scratch profile has no site: sqlite3 .../v-wizards/data/skotiq.db -> observer_latitude|0.0, observer_longitude|0.0, observer_elevation|0.0, and the Equipment readiness rail actively flags 'No observing location set' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-16.png). (2) The startup path installs a real (0,0) location: /tmp/ns-audit/v-wizards/app.log line 17, 'Setting observer location: lat=0, lon=0, elev=0', emitted by set_observer_location in native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/state.rs:355-364. (3) The native guard the finding names is therefore dead code in this state: polar_align/mod.rs:389-399 only fails when ctx.latitude/longitude are None AND device_ops.get_observer_location() returns None - with (0,0) installed it returns Some((0.0,0.0)) and the wizard proceeds. (4) The Dart pre-flight has no site check: polar_alignment_screen.dart:59-120 (_startAlignment) validates camera connection, mount connection and plateSolveServiceProvider.ensureSolverAvailable(), then starts - nothing about the observing site. (5) Live: I started All-Sky polar alignment with no site set and it ran, plate-solved and entered the adjust phase (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-28.png), i.e. it is not refused. The az/alt decomposition of a polar-axis error is latitude-dependent, so the corrections printed are for an equatorial observer. P1 stands.

verdicts.title: An aborted polar alignment is written to Alignment History as a success with a green "+97%" improvement badge
verdicts.location_wrong: Symptom and file are right, but one styling detail in the evidence is wrong: the finding says the 1376" row carried a GREEN checkmark. _history_panel.dart:222-227 colours the icon `entry.finalTotalError < 60 ? colors.success : colors.warning`, so at 1376" that tick renders AMBER, not green. The green element at that value is only the improvement badge (`improvementPercent > 50 ? colors.success : colors.info`, :245-259). A fixer should not go hunting for an unconditional green tick - the tick is already error-graded; it is the ICON SHAPE (autoCompleted ? target : check - a cancelled run still gets a checkmark) and the badge that lie.
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced with my own run and my own numbers. All-Sky -> Start Alignment, let it plate-solve 11 iterations against the simulators without touching anything (a simulator has no bolts to turn), then pressed Stop. Footer read 'Polar alignment stopped' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-29.png) - and a row was still committed: sqlite3 .../polar_alignment_history -> 1|523.692587689665|0.0|0|1785687175|1785687293, i.e. auto_completed=0 with completed_at populated. The Alignment History panel (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-30.png) then rendered 'Today 12:14 / Final: 0"' with a green checkmark and a green '+100%' badge, for a run the user cancelled and in which nothing was adjusted. The improvement figure is exactly the artefact the finding describes: my series ran 31421.6" -> 95942.4" -> 0.0" -> ... -> 16688.0" (app.log, 'All-sky polar align: total='), pure sample noise, and 'initial' is just whichever noisy sample landed first. Persistence-on-cancel is deliberate in source: polar_alignment_provider.dart stopAlignment() calls _saveHistoryOnce() at :717-733 with autoCompleted defaulting to false, and the history panel has no 'stopped' presentation at all. P1 held.

verdicts.title: Polar alignment ends with a green "Alignment Complete" tick and a green "+0%" chip after a 30-arcminute residual error
verdicts.location_wrong: The completion half of the finding is exactly located (polar_alignment_screen_parts/_completion_panel.dart). The HISTORY half is wrong and I disproved it by pixel: the finding says the 1800" history row is 'stamped with a green checkmark ... +0%'. It is not. _history_panel.dart:222-227 grades the tick `finalTotalError < 60 ? colors.success : colors.warning` and :245-259 grades the badge `improvementPercent > 50 ? colors.success : colors.info`, so at 1800"/+0% the row renders an AMBER tick and a BLUE badge - see the 3x crop /tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-34b.png, where my 1800" row is amber+blue directly above a 0"/+100% row that is green+green. A fixer told 'the history row is green' would change already-correct code.
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced the completion screen end to end. Simulated Camera + Mount connected, Imaging -> Mount -> Three-Point Polar Alignment -> TPPA -> Start Alignment; three points measured and solved (app.log 'Capturing point 3/3', 'Calculating polar alignment error'), adjust phase entered with the rail reading Az 1412.4" / Alt -1603.0" / Total 2136.5" in red, then I pressed Done. /tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-33.png: a large green success check, headline 'Alignment Complete', 'Final error: 1800.0 arcseconds', Alignment Summary 'Before 1800" -> After 1800"', and an Improvement chip rendered '+0%' in green. DB confirms the app knew better: select initial_total_error,final_total_error,auto_completed from polar_alignment_history -> row 2 = 1800.00129188552|1800.00131984104|0, i.e. auto_completed=0 and the residual got very slightly WORSE. 1800" = 30 arcmin = 60x the wizard's own 30" auto-complete threshold. Source is unconditional: _completion_panel.dart _buildCompleteStatus() always paints Icon(SkotiqIcons.success, color: colors.success) + 'Alignment Complete', and _buildCompletionSummary() always paints the improvement badge with SkotiqDecorations.tintedBadge(colors.success) and text colour colors.success - no threshold or sign test anywhere (only the thin progress bar behind it is graded). P1 held.

verdicts.title: Flat Frame Wizard captures at a different camera offset than the Imaging screen (10 vs 50) and never shows which gain/offset it will use
verdicts.reasoning: Both halves reproduced in one session on one camera. Imaging -> Camera tab reads 'Gain (0-600) 100' and 'Offset (0-255) 50' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-35.png). The light-frame path on the same camera minutes earlier: app.log 16:09:40 'Starting 120s exposure with gain=Some(100), offset=Some(50), bin=1x1'. The Flat Frame Wizard Quick Capture run on the same camera: seven consecutive lines 16:25:58-16:26:xx 'Starting <t>s exposure with gain=Some(100), offset=Some(10), bin=1x1'. So lights get offset 50 and flats get offset 10 in the same session - a different bias pedestal, which the app's own matcher then rejects (flat_library_dao.dart:132, gain/offset/binning must match exactly). The UI half is also true: the Quick Capture panel shows only Filter, Histogram Target, Tolerance and Frame Count (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-37.png) - no gain, no offset, no override. Cited location is right and I pinned the divergence: flat_wizard_service.dart:321 `offset = profileDefaultOffset ?? currentOffset ?? status?.offset`, fed from flat_wizard_provider.dart:144-149 (profile?.defaultOffset, camera.offset). In this profile equipment_profiles.default_offset is NULL (sqlite3 -> '1|My Equipment||') so it falls through to the camera's live/driver-reported offset (10), while the light path uses app_settings default_offset=50. Two sources of truth, exactly as the finding says. P1 held.

verdicts.title: Flat wizard Quick Capture ignores the selected filter and always drives the wheel to position 0
verdicts.duplicate_of: Overlaps 'Flat wizard cannot capture a flat when a filter move is needed' - the failure the reporter actually saw is that finding's confirmation-loop timeout, misattributed to filter selection.
verdicts.reasoning: I ran the exact stated repro and the wizard drove to the SELECTED filter, not to 0. Imaging -> clicked the Ha chip; app.log 16:18:47 'api_filterwheel_set_position ... position=4' (Ha). Then Camera tab -> Flat Wizard -> Quick Capture, opened the Filter dropdown (entries L,R,G,B,Ha,OIII,SII with Ha selected, /tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-38.png), chose B, header strip updated to 'FILTER B' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-40.png), pressed Start Capture and gave it a folder. app.log 16:20:43: '[API] api_filterwheel_set_position called: device_id=sim_filterwheel_1, position=3'. B is the 4th entry, so position 3 is exactly right - it is NOT 0. The follow-on error banner also named the right filter and the right index: 'B: filter wheel did not confirm position 3 within 15s - run stopped.' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-44.png), not 'L ... position 0'. I also tested the other reading of the report - reopening the wizard and pressing Start WITHOUT touching the dropdown (it defaulted to Ha, the app's believed wheel position): that run issued no set_position at all, because the move-skip branch fired; again not position 0. The 'Filter dropdown is decorative / always targets index 0' claim does not hold in this build. What the reporter did see is real, but it is the 15s confirmation timeout of the other finding; the 'L / position 0' labelling in their evidence is not reproducible here.

verdicts.title: Flat wizard cannot capture a flat when a filter move is needed - its wheel move neither takes effect nor is confirmed, while the same move works from Equipment
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced with the wheel at Ha and the wizard asked for B. app.log 16:20:43.804816 '[API] api_filterwheel_set_position called: device_id=sim_filterwheel_1, position=3' immediately followed at 16:20:43.804835 by '[API] Filter wheel position set successfully' - and 15 s later the wizard failed closed: 'B: filter wheel did not confirm position 3 within 15s - run stopped.' with the run strip flipping to Failed (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-44.png). The asymmetry the finding claims is real and I verified it both directions: driving the SAME wheel from the Imaging filter chip row worked (position=4 commanded at 16:18:47, and the chip row plus the wizard's own dropdown both then showed Ha), whereas after the wizard's move the app still believed the wheel was on Ha (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-46.png, Ha chip still lit; /tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-47.png, the reopened wizard defaulting to Ha) even though the driver had accepted position 3. Cited root cause is precisely right, and I found the counterpart that proves it: DeviceService's changeFilter path calls _verifyFilterWheelPosition (control_helpers.dart:314-361), which polls `_backend.getFilterWheelStatus(deviceId)` and pushes the result into the provider via filterWheelNotifier.updatePosition/setMoving - while flat_wizard_provider.dart:1351-1382 calls deviceBackend.filterWheelSetPosition directly and then polls `ref.read(filterWheelStateProvider)` in a loop, with nothing in that loop ever fetching status. The provider can therefore never change and the wait always expires. Outcome matches too: zero flats written (find /tmp/ns-audit/v-wizards/flats -type f -> 0 files; select count(*) from flat_history -> 0). Worse than reported: the stale state also makes the NEXT run unsafe - my second run skipped the move because the app still thought it was on Ha, and exposed seven frames labelled Ha while the driver was on position 3 (B). P1 held (P0-adjacent only because that second run happened to die on ADU convergence before saving anything).

verdicts.title: Co-imaging card says "You are pooling light here" after you explicitly decline to share your subs
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced against a real hub I stood up myself (dart run bin/server.dart --port 8093 --bind 127.0.0.1 --db /tmp/ns-audit/hub-vw/hub.db). Connected the app, pressed Start session, created NGC 7000 at RA 314.75 / Dec 44.31. The 'Share your co-imaging subs' dialog opened with both consent boxes unchecked ('Let this rig contribute my completed subs unattended ... Leave unchecked and your subs will NOT be added to the combined stack' and 'I understand this shares my completed subs under the license above'). I pressed Cancel. The session card then rendered a green check with 'You are pooling light here', COMBINED 0s, FRAMES 0, RIGS 1 (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-56.png). I checked the hub's own state rather than trusting the app: select count(*) from consent_records -> 0, select count(*) from contributions -> 0. So the claim is false on the server's books as well as the user's intent. STRONGER than reported in one respect: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-55.png shows the caption already rendered behind the still-open consent dialog, i.e. it does not even wait for the answer. Cited location is right: coimaging_session_card.dart:371-390, `if (joined == true)` -> checkCircle2 in colors.success + 'You are pooling light here', with no reference to sharing/consent state. P1 held.

verdicts.title: The collaborative mosaic detail screen is a nav trap: no back control, and the whole nav rail stops working
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced against my own hub (127.0.0.1:8093) after seeding one collaborative mosaic. Plan Tonight -> Discover -> Collaborate -> 'View panels' on the M31 Wide Field row pushes a full-screen detail page titled 'M31 Wide Field / Collaborative mosaic - panels split across the club' whose header carries ONLY a refresh icon - no back arrow, no breadcrumb (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-59.png). From there: clicked Dashboard in the left rail -> the rail repainted Dashboard as the selected destination (accent bar and all) while the mosaic detail stayed fully rendered (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-60.png). Then clicked Imaging and pressed Escape, Alt+Left, BackSpace and the mouse back button in turn -> rail now shows Imaging selected, mosaic detail still on screen (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/wiz-61.png). So both halves hold, including the nastiest part: the app refuses to navigate AND misreports where you are. Cited location is correct on both counts - collaborative_sky_screen.dart:690-697 pushes `MaterialPageRoute<void>(builder: (_) => CollabMosaicDetailScreen(...))` via Navigator.of(context), and CollabMosaicDetailScreen (collab_mosaic_detail_screen.dart:33-56) is a bare Scaffold whose ScreenHeader takes only title/subtitle/icon/trailing - screen_header.dart:8-22 has no leading or back slot at all, so no back control is even expressible there. P1 held: there is still an escape path (Join mosaic -> project screen breadcrumb) and nothing is lost, which keeps it off P0.
